title: Joining the musicians' union and Don Albert
summary: He recalls joining the union around 1928, Tats Alexander, and the band passing to Dwight Newman and Don Albert.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: No, the union wasn't so very active around in the early parts of the twenties. I think I first joined the union in 19…let's see, I went into 1928, something like that. When George Augustine and formerly old bass player, and I forget that other man used to play a band, Willie Bontem. Oh, yeah. I met him once. Yeah, Willie Bontem. We sat at the old St. Catherine Hall on Tulane Avenue, I believe in South Villiers, somewhere up in the neighborhood. Yeah, the old St. Catherine Hall. It's still there. It's still there, yeah. It's what he was the president. In later years, the headquarters move over to, after the junk hotel on us, they call it now LaSalle Street, where the old man, Tats, daddy was janitor over there, he was our recording financial secretary. We used to call him in them days. The old man, I'm trying to think of his name now. He used to play the peck horn, the door baritone, you know, in all the funeral bands. Like old man Barberang used to play, you know, the alto horn. Yeah. And then we had, from that band… Wasn't named the Alexanders, I guess. That was Alexanders, yeah. Yeah, old man. But we had a nickname we used to call him. That's Tats. His right name is, Tats playing side, his right name is Adolf Alexander, but they all called him Tats for nickname.
Yeah. Did his father have a nickname?

Yeah, that's what I'm trying to think now. His father's nickname used to call him, I can't think of a president name. But anyhow, he was, I was financial secretary of the local. And then we kept that organization until Bush died. Then Dwight Newman, the piano player, he took the band over. And then we first, the man we had to place, Bush Hall, was a fellow by the name of Albert Dominick, known as Don Alick. Oh, yeah. Don Albert, yeah. I think he's now living in El Paso, Texas. In later years he formed a big large dance, you know, dance band. He made some records too. Yeah, he called us Don Albert's Arbistry, but he's from New Orleans, used to live on Robinson and St. Anthony. But he was…
We must try to remember to talk to his father is still living here. He's still living here.
Ferdinand, I believe his name is Ferdinand. Yeah, old cigar maker. And I knew Danny Dominick in Chicago, right? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
